scope.summary: Establish Stage's typed SurrealDB storage foundation, shared application-bootstrap handle, SCHEMAFULL SurrealKit rollouts, EventLedger boundary, ArtifactStore references, browser-profile materialization boundary, and real-database proof harness before feature lanes persist state.
forbidden_paths: Turso/libSQL/SQLite/PostgreSQL product, runtime, test, fixture, cache, fallback, compatibility, migration, import, reconciliation, or proof paths
acceptance_criteria: A single application-bootstrap embedded SurrealStorage handle is injected into a typed StageRepository; no production Stage feature opens a private database or calls feature-local open_default().

Stage-owned durable records use typed SCHEMAFULL SurrealDB tables with assertions, indexes, authenticated record-user permissions, and ordered SurrealKit rollouts; EventLedger records attributable durable transitions.

ArtifactStore remains authoritative for bytes/manifests/hashes/retention/materialization, while browser-engine profile files remain isolated non-canonical runtime materialization; Stage backup restores SurrealDB records and ArtifactHandles before profiles.

Real WP-scoped embedded SurrealDB tests prove clean bootstrap, reopen/restart, parallel writers, idempotency/conflict behavior, permission isolation, interrupted rollout recovery, and database-outage behavior.
Fresh zero-match guards prove Stage has no Turso, libSQL, SQLite, PostgreSQL, feature-private database, fallback, dual-write, mock-only, or in-memory-only authority path.

requirements: Open the canonical Handshake-managed embedded SurrealDB once at application bootstrap and inject a typed StageRepository; production Stage code must not use feature-local open_default().
Define Stage-owned SCHEMAFULL tables, indexes, assertions, authenticated record-user permissions, and SurrealKit rollouts without reading or mutating another subsystem's private tables.
Use EventLedger for attributable durable transitions; keep ArtifactStore authoritative for bytes/manifests/hashes/retention/materialization and retain only opaque ArtifactHandles plus Stage lineage.
Keep cookies, cache, local storage, IndexedDB, service workers, DRM state, and similar browser-engine profile materialization isolated on disk and non-canonical for product backup/restore.
Reject Turso, libSQL, SQLite, PostgreSQL, private database engines, fallback/dual-write paths, mock-only proof, and in-memory-only proof.
proof_when_applicable: real WP-scoped embedded SurrealDB bootstrap and reopen test
SurrealKit SCHEMAFULL rollout, assertion, index, and authenticated record-user permission proof
parallel StageRepository writer and deterministic conflict/idempotency proof
database outage and interrupted rollout recovery proof
zero-match guard for forbidden database dependencies, drivers, URLs, migrations, fixtures, caches, fallbacks, and compatibility paths

surfaces: Stage storage health and schema identity projection when operator-visible
gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: The storage foundation is backend-first; if no operator-visible health surface changes in this MT, record typed NOT_APPLICABLE evidence and bind the later diagnostics projection MT.

hbr_obligations: HBR-PRIV authenticated record-user permission proof for every Stage table
HBR portability: runtime roots are config-derived and disk-agnostic
hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: Tier-1 structured storage health, rollout identity, outage diagnostics, and reproduction steps

risks: A Stage-private database would fork product authority and create cross-store capture/job recovery gaps.
Multiple feature-local SurrealStorage opens could diverge configuration, rollout state, or connection lifecycle even when they point at the same path.
Browser profile files could be mistaken for canonical product records or backup authority.
Mock-only storage tests could pass while embedded SurrealDB permissions, rollouts, restart behavior, or concurrency fail.
Parallel remediation branches may expose incompatible storage modules or schema registries at the activation baseline.
minimum_controls: One application-owned injected storage handle and typed StageRepository boundary.
SCHEMAFULL SurrealKit rollouts with authenticated record-user permissions and real embedded database proof.
ArtifactStore and browser-profile boundaries are explicit and fault-injected.
L00 binds the reconciled WP-KERNEL-012 and WP-1 Multi-Model Orchestration SurrealDB baseline before implementation.
Forbidden-database and feature-private-open zero-match guards are release-blocking.
